findings.title: `getLoginPredicate()` returns false for enabled IDPs linked to a disabled organization
findings.body: In `update(IdentityProviderModel model)`, `original` is retrieved via `getById(model.getInternalId())`, which wraps the cached model in `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel` (line 432). That wrapper overrides `isEnabled()` to return `false` whenever the linked organization is currently disabled. Because `LoginFilter.ENABLED` calls `IdentityProviderModel::isEnabled`, `getLoginPredicate().test(original)` evaluates to `false` for an enabled IDP if its organization happens to be disabled at the time of the update. Conversely, `getForLogin` queries `idpDelegate.getForLogin(...)` in JPA, which checks the IDP's own `enabled` column without checking the organization's `enabled` state, so IDPs of disabled organizations ARE stored in the `getForLogin` cache (and filtered later by `OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean`). If an IDP is added, removed, or updated while its organization is disabled (e.g., changing `hideOnLogin` or unlinking it from the disabled organization), `getLoginPredicate()` wrongly concludes the IDP is not a login IDP and skips invalidating the login caches. Once the organization is re-enabled, `getForLogin` will serve stale cached IDP lists.

findings.title: Test cleanup registers literal `"alias"` instead of the created IDP alias
findings.body: At lines 381 and 425 of `testCacheIDPForLogin`, the cleanup handler is registered as `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove);` using the literal string `"alias"` instead of the actual alias of the created identity provider (`"idp-alias-" + i` and `"idp-alias-20"`). None of the 20 created identity providers are removed after the test finishes (and cleanup will fail with a 404 trying to delete `"alias"`), leaking test data into subsequent tests in the class.
